s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bony mass of the forehead
salient_findings: Painless, slowly progressive mass on the left forehead
Diffuse sclerosis and intra-trabecular fibrosis on core biopsy
key_facts: 45-year-old man
History of systemic lupus erythematosus, well controlled
No immunomodulatory therapy
30 × 20 mm mass on the left forehead
Mass progressed over 1 year
Previous excision of a similar frontal bone lesion
Previous lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia
No headaches or neurologic symptoms
CT scan showed homogenous matrix expansion of the frontal bone
Fine-needle aspiration cytology excluded multiple myeloma
Core biopsy demonstrated diffuse sclerosis and intra-trabecular fibrosis
Preoperative laboratory tests were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Previous diagnosis of fibrous dysplasia and current biopsy findings suggestive of fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Monostotic fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Single bone involvement and previous diagnosis of fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive bony mass of the forehead and radiographic findings of homogenous matrix expansion

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic findings of ground-glass appearance and homogenous matrix expansion

shortlist.label: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: History of systemic lupus erythematosus and previous diagnosis of fibrous dysplasia, with possibility of multiple bone involvement

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of a similar lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia, and the current lesion's characteristics, such as homogenous matrix expansion of the frontal bone and core biopsy findings of diffuse sclerosis and intra-trabecular fibrosis, are consistent with fibrous dysplasia. The fact that it is localized to one bone (frontal bone) suggests monostotic rather than polyostotic fibrous dysplasia.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Too broad, as it does not specify the extent of bone involvement

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Typically presents with bilateral involvement of the mandible and maxilla, which is not the case here

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Usually has a more heterogeneous appearance on imaging and does not typically show the ground-glass appearance seen in this patient

rejected.label: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Involves multiple bones, which is not indicated in this patient's history or current presentation
